note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every court count, address, opening time and lighting mark below comes from one page published by the Austin Parks and Recreation Department, which calls it the list of official Department pickleball locations. The same page carries a separate section of indoor courts inside recreation centres; that section is real, is not yet verified, and is named below rather than left out.

slots.parking: Austin publishes nothing about parking at any of these twenty-one venues. Two things are worth knowing before you drive. The Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center requires a reservation, so arriving without one is a wasted trip. Hancock Recreation Center closes its court to open play between 2:30 p.m. and 6:30 p.m. on term-time weekdays. At the pocket parks, expect street parking, though the City does not say so.
slots.peak_hours: Fifteen of the twenty-one venues run the same schedule: "Open Play: 7 Days a Week, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m." The exceptions are where the useful information is. At Pan American Neighborhood Park the City states that courts are unavailable Tuesday and Thursday from 7 to 10 p.m. and at weekends from 9 a.m. to noon, for roller derby. Austin High Tennis Center shares its courts with Austin Independent School District: weekday evenings from 5:30 p.m. during term, seven days a week in summer. Hancock closes midday on term-time weekdays. South Austin opens at 8 a.m. rather than 7.
slots.surface_condition: No surface is stated at any Austin venue. The City describes what a court is striped for, not what it is made of. Thirty-nine of Austin's sixty verified courts are lines painted onto a multi-purpose slab shared with other sports, and twenty-one are dedicated pickleball. Every venue reads "not verified yet" on surface.
slots.local_scene: Austin is the first city in this directory whose operator answers the lighting question at scale in prose. Eleven of these twenty-one venues carry the words "Lighted during park hours", and in a city where summer play happens after sunset that is the most useful fact on the page. It is also one of the operators in this directory that states that a net is NOT provided: Brentwood and Balcones say "bring your own portable net", and Rosewood and Springwoods say "Nets not included."

best_for.heading: Best if you want a real pickleball facility
best_for.text: The Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center at Walnut Creek Sports Park has eight outdoor pickleball courts, by some distance the largest count in the city and more than three times the Austin average. It is lit during park hours and open Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 10 p.m., weekends 8:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. It is also the only Austin venue the City marks "Reservations Required" rather than Open Play, so book before you go. No price is published on the pickleball page.

best_for.heading: Best if you are playing after dark
best_for.text: Eleven of Austin's twenty-one venues are lit, so this is a real choice rather than a single option. Dick Nichols District Park is the pick on count: five pickleball courts striped onto two multi-purpose courts, lit during park hours, open seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. If you are closer to the centre, Pan American and Rosewood are lit too, but check Pan American's roller derby schedule first.

best_for.heading: Best if you want pickleball and nothing else
best_for.text: Twenty-one of Austin's sixty courts are dedicated pickleball rather than lines on a shared slab. Pan American Neighborhood Park has three of them plus one striped court, lit, close to downtown on Chicon St. The catch is on the same page: the courts are unavailable Tuesday and Thursday evenings and weekend mornings from 9 a.m. for roller derby practice. South Austin Neighborhood Park's two dedicated courts, also lit, are the simpler option if that schedule does not suit.

best_for.heading: Best to know before you pack
best_for.text: Three Austin venues tell you outright that a net is not provided: Brentwood and Balcones say bring your own portable net, and Rosewood and Springwoods say "Nets not included." Rosewood is the one worth knowing about because it is otherwise among the better venues in the city: four courts, two of them dedicated, lit during park hours, open 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Bring a net and it is one of Austin's best. For the other eighteen venues the City says nothing about nets either way.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Austin have?
faqs.a: Sixty verified courts across twenty-one City of Austin venues, all outdoor. That makes Austin one of the largest cities in this directory by court count. A twenty-second outdoor location, Balcones District Park, is not published: its entry gives no court number and the geocoder cannot match its address.

Eleven of the twenty-one: Austin High Tennis Center, the Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center, Beverly S. Sheffield, Brentwood, Dick Nichols, Little Zilker, Pan American, Patterson, Rosewood, Shipe and South Austin. The City marks each one "Lighted during park hours". The other ten carry no lighting statement, which means unknown rather than dark.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: At Brentwood, Rosewood and Springwoods, yes. The City says so in words: "bring your own portable net" and "Nets not included." At the other eighteen venues the City says nothing either way.

faqs.q: Can I book a court, and is it free?
faqs.a: Booking is at one venue only. The Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center is marked "Reservations Required"; every other entry says Open Play. Across the whole of this directory only a handful of other venues take bookings, so an Austin reservation is a genuinely unusual thing. Cost is not verified anywhere: Austin states no price on its pickleball page.

faqs.q: Are there indoor courts in Austin?
faqs.a: Yes, and they are not yet verified. The City's page has a second section, "Pickleball Programming at Rec Centers", listing indoor courts at Austin, Dittmar, Dove Springs, Gus Garcia, Montopolis, Northwest, Parque Zaragoza and South Austin recreation centres, with open-play session times.

sources.evidence: The City's pickleball page, introduced as "The list below represents official Austin Parks and Recreation Department pickleball locations:" and carrying, per venue, a street address, a court count, opening hours and, at eleven venues, "Lighted during park hours". Also "Reservations Required" at the Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center; "bring your own portable net" at Brentwood and Balcones; "Nets not included." at Rosewood and Springwoods; "Courts unavailable on Tuesday and Thursday from 7 to 10 p.m. and Saturday and Sunday from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. for roller derby practice" at Pan American; the AISD sharing agreement at Austin High; and the separate "Pickleball Programming at Rec Centers" section. Every published address was matched by the Census address geocoder and placed in the incorporated place "Austin city": nineteen in Travis County and two in Williamson. 12017 Amherst Dr returned no match, which is one of the two grounds for excluding Balcones District Park. The geocoder also returns a different postcode from the City's page at two venues: 78721 against the City's 78702 at Eastside Pocket Park, and 78717 against 78753 at North Lake Creek.
